symbols.name: ground set size
symbols.meaning: The number of elements of the ground set $[h]=\{1,\dots,h\}$, a count.
symbols.quote: Let $[h]=\{1,\dots,h\}$ be the ground set, whose size is $h$.

symbols.name: triples
symbols.meaning: The set of all three-element subsets of the ground set.
symbols.quote: Let $\mathcal T$ be the set of all triples.

symbols.name: triple S
symbols.meaning: A triple, one of the letters that always denote triples on this page.
symbols.quote: The letters $S$ and $T$ always denote three-element subsets of $[h]$, called *triples*.

symbols.name: triple T
symbols.meaning: A triple, one of the letters that always denote triples on this page.
symbols.quote: The letters $S$ and $T$ always denote three-element subsets of $[h]$, called *triples*.

symbols.name: bank index
symbols.meaning: A triple of triples $(\Psi_1,\Psi_2,\Psi_3)$ that indexes one entry of a bank.
symbols.quote: A *bank* is a family of scalars indexed by $\Psi=(\Psi_1,\Psi_2,\Psi_3)\in\mathcal T^3$.

symbols.name: source bank
symbols.meaning: The bank of scalars that the exchange reads from.
symbols.quote: The network has two banks $X$ and $Y$, with entries $X_\Psi$ and $Y_\Psi$.

symbols.name: target bank
symbols.meaning: The bank of scalars that the exchange writes to.
symbols.quote: The network has two banks $X$ and $Y$, with entries $X_\Psi$ and $Y_\Psi$.

symbols.name: side wire
symbols.meaning: The wire attached to an ordered neighbouring pair $(S,T)$.
symbols.quote: Each ordered neighbouring pair $(S,T)$ has a *side wire* $A_{ST}$, and each ground element $\Upsilon\in[h]$ has a *central wire* $C_\Upsilon$.

symbols.name: central wire
symbols.meaning: The wire attached to a ground element $\Upsilon$.
symbols.quote: Each ordered neighbouring pair $(S,T)$ has a *side wire* $A_{ST}$, and each ground element $\Upsilon\in[h]$ has a *central wire* $C_\Upsilon$.

symbols.name: ground element
symbols.meaning: An element of the ground set $[h]$, which indexes a central wire.
symbols.quote: Each ordered neighbouring pair $(S,T)$ has a *side wire* $A_{ST}$, and each ground element $\Upsilon\in[h]$ has a *central wire* $C_\Upsilon$.

symbols.name: starting side values
symbols.meaning: The starting values of the side wires, which the network must restore.
symbols.quote: Let $A^0$ and $C^0$ be the starting values of the side wires and the central wires.

symbols.name: starting central values
symbols.meaning: The starting values of the central wires, which the network must restore.
symbols.quote: Let $A^0$ and $C^0$ be the starting values of the side wires and the central wires.

symbols.name: indicator vector
symbols.meaning: The $0/1$ vector in $E$ whose ones mark the three elements of $T$.
symbols.quote: Let $t_T$ be the $0/1$ indicator vector of $T$.

symbols.name: bilinear space
symbols.meaning: The fixed bilinear space whose subspaces are the labels; the letter $E$ changes meaning here.
symbols.quote: The network labels its wires with [subspace labels](subspace-labels.md): nondegenerate subspaces of a fixed bilinear space $E$.

symbols.name: all-ones matrix
symbols.meaning: The $h\times h$ matrix whose entries are all $1$.
symbols.quote: For the bit network take $E=\mathbb Q^h$ with the form $\langle\mathbf p,\mathbf q\rangle=\mathbf p^{\mathsf T}(I-J/9)\mathbf q$, where $\mathbf p,\mathbf q$ are vectors of $E$ and $J$ is the all-ones matrix.

symbols.name: first form vector
symbols.meaning: A vector of $E$ in the form $\langle\mathbf p,\mathbf q\rangle$.
symbols.quote: For the bit network take $E=\mathbb Q^h$ with the form $\langle\mathbf p,\mathbf q\rangle=\mathbf p^{\mathsf T}(I-J/9)\mathbf q$, where $\mathbf p,\mathbf q$ are vectors of $E$ and $J$ is the all-ones matrix.

symbols.name: second form vector
symbols.meaning: A vector of $E$ in the form $\langle\mathbf p,\mathbf q\rangle$.
symbols.quote: For the bit network take $E=\mathbb Q^h$ with the form $\langle\mathbf p,\mathbf q\rangle=\mathbf p^{\mathsf T}(I-J/9)\mathbf q$, where $\mathbf p,\mathbf q$ are vectors of $E$ and $J$ is the all-ones matrix.

relations.quote: The network labels its wires with [subspace labels](subspace-labels.md): nondegenerate subspaces of a fixed bilinear space $E$.

relations.predicate: is built within the framework of
relations.quote: The network is built within the framework of [Linear networks and frames](linear-network-frames.md), in which each wire is a role and each vertex carries a frame.
The labels' orthogonality and nondegeneracy are tested with the [bilinear form](bilinear-form.md) of $E$.
Nondegeneracy is checked through the [Eigenvalue](eigenvalue.md)s of the form matrix $I-J/9$.
Edge residuals are computed through the [Dual space](dual-space.md) $U'^{*}$, the linear functionals on $U'$.
